The pizza that never gets old.
A new type of food packaging could help keep pizzas fresh for up to a year, according to researchers at the University of Illinois. Their work is published in ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces .
Pizzas are typically stored and transported on cardboard trays or plastic containers with lids made from polyethylene terephthalate (PET), which can be recycled but also leaches chemicals into foods over time. In this study, scientists wanted to see if they could create an alternative material using PET waste byproducts called glycolic acid oligomers . These materials have been used as coatings before — including one developed last month , based off similar technology — so it was worth exploring whether these compounds might make good replacements too.
To test their idea out, the team created two types of films: One had 10 percent weight percentage of glycolic acids while another contained only water molecules; both were then coated onto aluminum foil sheets. They found that when exposed to air moisture levels above about five parts per million, each film began breaking down after just three days under normal room conditions without any additional heat applied during storage periods ranging between six months all the way through nine years! This means there’s no need worry anymore because now we know how long our favorite pies will stay delicious even though nobody wants them getting stale!
This research has potential applications beyond simply keeping your favourite slice safe until you’re ready eat again – think shipping perishable goods across continents quickly enough not spoil en route thanks some sort-of magic coating designed specifically around preserving freshness rather than protecting against contamination like traditional plastics do today

Abstract—The genera C era t o c y st i si s , S p h e r u losphe ra ceae an d Nectriales are important pathogens on woody plants worldwide; however they have been poorly studied in Asia. In this study we report two novel fungal taxa that belong to these three families based upon morphological characteristics as well as molecular data obtained by ITS sequences analysis. The first one is named Cerato cysti s fuscata gen . et comb ., which was collected from diseased leaves of Quercus acutissima Blume ex Hildebr., while the second taxon belongs to Sphear ulosphaerae fam . nov.; it has been found growing inside bark tissues of Pinus tabulaeformis Carr.. Both fungi were identified using DNA barcoding techniques with internal transcribed spacer region sequence analyses. This paper provides information about their morphology and phylogenetic relationships within each family. These findings will contribute towards our understanding of plant pathogenicity caused by members belonging to different classes of Ascomycota .

Three things to know before Thursday's first round of the draft.
1. The Rams are in position for a quarterback, but they're not going after one with their No. 14 pick:
The Los Angeles Rams have been linked closely to Oklahoma State signal-caller Mason Rudolph and Washington passer Jake Browning as potential selections at No. 13 or even earlier than that if teams trade up ahead of them -- which is likely given how much interest there has been on both quarterbacks this offseason.
But it seems unlikely either will be available when L.A.'s turn comes around because Cleveland (No. 4), Arizona (5) and Denver (6) all could use an upgrade under center while Miami (7) would love another playmaker alongside Ryan Tannehill .
2. There should still be plenty of value left by the time the Chargers select third overall: 
San Diego owns three picks inside the top five thanks to trades made last year involving Philip Rivers , Melvin Ingram and Keenan Allen . But those deals also cost general manager Tom Telesco his second-rounder from each transaction so he'll only get two more chances to add talent until next April.
That means whoever falls into San Diego’s lap between Nos. 3 through 12 won't necessarily represent a steal like Joey Bosa did back then; however, you can bet your bottom dollar someone who goes off the board early Friday night isn’t getting away without being paid handsomely down the road.
3. It wouldn't surprise me if the Browns take Baker Mayfield over Sam Darnold :
Browns coach Hue Jackson said Monday during his pre-draft press conference that "it doesn't matter" whether Ohio native Josh Rosen ends up wearing orange-and-brown instead of purple-and-gold come Week One since neither player was drafted out of UCLA where they played together just months ago.
Jackson added later Tuesday morning via Twitter : “I think we’re gonna do what I feel best fits our team.”
So unless something changes drastically leading right up till kickoff tonight, expect the former Heisman Trophy winner to go fourth overall regardless of whom else winds up taking him home.

Abstract—The genera C era t o c y st i si s , S p h e r u losphe ra ceae an d Nectriales are important pathogens on woody plants worldwide; however they have been poorly studied in Asia. In this study we report two novel fungal taxa that belong to these three families based upon morphological characteristics as well as molecular data obtained by ITS sequences analysis. Dog’s Nose Can Detect Cancer, Study Finds | LiveScience.com - 2012-10-02
A dog named Max has a superpower: He is able to sniff out human cancers with an accuracy rate of up to 98 percent. The study was published in the journal PLoS ONE.
The researchers tested whether dogs could be trained to identify odors from people who had been diagnosed with bladder or prostate cancer and compared their results against those obtained by using urine samples collected at the same time as blood tests for these two types of tumors were performed on each person.
They found that when they asked volunteers’ spouses if there might have been any changes in smell before diagnosis — such as bad breath due to gum disease or body odor caused by sweating more than usual because of stress over work problems — only one spouse said yes; however this did not seem related either way since both men (who later developed lung cancer) reported no change whatsoever prior thereto!
Max also showed great promise but his performance wasn’t quite good enough yet – he scored just above chance level which means we need some further training sessions until our canine friend becomes reliable again!

Perovskites are materials that have been used successfully over several decades in high-temperature applications such as ceramics or catalysts because they can be made into solid solutions containing multiple elements. In recent years, however, scientists discovered their potential use in low-cost thin-film semiconductors suitable for optoelectronic device fabrication due to its tunable bandgap properties which allow it to absorb light across different wavelengths while also being highly stable against moisture and heat exposure during processing steps like sintering under vacuum conditions where other types of semiconductor cannot survive without degradation after prolonged periods away from ambient air environments.[1]
In this work we demonstrate how these unique features could potentially lead towards more sustainable energy generation technologies through our development of novel hybrid organic-inorganic halide perovskites based on methylammonium iodine bromides mixed crystals system MAPIxBr3-x(M=CH3NH4). We show here that when combined together within one single crystal lattice structure there exists strong interactions between both components leading them forming an intimate bond resulting not only enhanced stability but also improved performance compared traditional solution processed planar heterojunction type architectures currently employed today.”

But anyway here's my take.. If we assume that each time when they stop their engines are fully recharged so no need to consider fuel consumption during these times,
So basically what happens after stopping? They start again right away without waiting even one minute! So let me do some calculations based off those assumptions;
First part - From starting point till reaching destination = x hours * v + y minutes*v where 'x' represents number of complete whole hours traveled while 'y' represent remaining fraction of last completed full hour plus first incomplete half-hour; And since both values will always add up to exactly equaling total distance covered i.e., D=xy+v(x+½)
Second Part- After completing all trips within single calendar year including current ongoing run, Total Distance Covered would simply become sum of distances travelled per individual runs added together giving us final result being S=D+x(v+y)+D+(24-x)(V-Y)=S=(25-V)x+Y(26-v)-XY+Solving gives us Y=x-(5*v)/6 Now substituting back into original equation yields X=v*(3*y)/(4-y); Which means that average velocity over course of two consecutive journeys equals V=((7*x)+(8*z))/9 Where Z Represents Time Spent Refueling Engines Each Day As Well!
